sum: The Langtang Khola trail from Syabrubesi through forest and yak pasture to Kyanjin Gompa at 3,870 m, with a day hike to Kyanjin Ri or Tserko Ri before you walk back out.

guide.note: The Nepal Tourism Board has required foreign trekkers to hire a licensed guide since April 2023, though checks on the trail are inconsistent. Here a guide earns the fee twice over: by knowing which roadhead, bridges and lodges are in use after the 2026 flood, and by judging the weather and your condition on the Kyanjin Ri or Tserko Ri day.

access: Road only. Buses and jeeps leave Machhapokhari in Kathmandu early in the morning for Dhunche and Syabrubesi, seven to nine hours away on the Pasang Lhamu Highway. The Bhote Koshi flood of August 2026 cut the last section: as of November 2026 vehicles stop at Dhunche or Thulo Syabru and trekkers join the valley trail near Bamboo. Confirm the working roadhead before you book.

photo.a: The blue-roofed lodges of Kyanjin Gompa lie far below on a brown valley floor, with snow-covered mountainsides on the left and the upper Langtang valley running into the distance.
photo.c: Kyanjin Gompa and the upper Langtang valley from Kyanjin Ri

includes: porter in most packages (the cheapest tiers leave one out)
Langtang National Park permit and TIMS card
lodge beds and three meals a day on the trek
bus or shared jeep from Kathmandu and back

permits.name: Langtang National Park entry permit
permits.where: At the park checkpoint in Dhunche on the drive to Syabrubesi, or in advance at the Tourist Service Centre in Bhrikutimandap, Kathmandu.

permits.name: Trekkers' Information Management System card
permits.where: Only through a registered trekking agency, which applies in the Nepal Tourism Board's online system with your route and your guide's details. Individual trekkers can no longer buy one over the counter.

transportText: Bus or a jeep seat between Kathmandu and the Langtang roadhead, each way
tips: Bring enough rupees from Kathmandu for the whole trek. Do not count on finding a working ATM after Trishuli Bazaar.
Spend two nights at Kyanjin Gompa. With only one you either skip the day hike or walk it tired.
Lodges at Lama Hotel fill by mid-afternoon in October and November; Rimche, twenty minutes lower, usually has room.
Treat all water. Lodges sell boiled or filtered water, which saves buying plastic bottles.
Walk the path across the old village site quietly. Many of those who died in 2015 were never recovered, and their families run the lodges you sleep in.

days.note: A long road day through Trishuli Bazaar and Dhunche, where park permits are checked. Since the August 2026 flood, vehicles have been stopping at Dhunche or Thulo Syabru instead; settle the roadhead with your agency before you book transport.

Cross the Bhote Koshi, then follow the Langtang Khola upstream through a damp gorge of oak, maple and bamboo. Lunch at Bamboo; the last two hours, up to Rimche and along to Lama Hotel, are the steepest. If you start from Thulo Syabru instead, you join this trail a little below Bamboo.

Forest for three hours to the checkpost at Ghodatabela, then the valley widens into yak pasture. You gain 960 m of sleeping height, the most of the trek; if a headache starts, stop at Thangshyap. The trail crosses the 2015 debris field just before the rebuilt village.

A short morning past Mundu and long mani walls, climbing gently over old moraine. Arrive for lunch, then spend the afternoon on your feet around the gompa and the cheese factory rather than lying down; it helps you adjust.

days.t: Day hike to Kyanjin Ri or Tserko Ri
days.note: Kyanjin Ri is the usual choice: a steep 900 m climb to 4,773 m and back by lunch. Tserko Ri, at 4,984 m, is higher and much longer, seven to eight hours return; take it on only if you slept well, and start by 6 am. Turn back if cloud closes in.
The whole upper valley in reverse, downhill almost all the way. It is easy on the lungs and hard on knees and toes, so use poles. Lunch at Thangshyap or Ghodatabela.

Back down the gorge to the road. For a change of scene, take the high trail from Rimche through Sherpagaon and Khangjim, which stays in the sun and adds an hour or two. While the Syabrubesi road is closed, turn off below Bamboo for Thulo Syabru instead.
The same road in reverse. Landslides and roadworks make the timing unpredictable, so do not book an international flight for the same evening.
